problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-8x-3?$

feedback.problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=3{x}^{6}-7{x}^{5}+8{x}^{3}-4x+2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $2,$ and the leading coefficient is $3.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }2}{\text{factor of }3}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $-1=\frac{-1}{1}$ takes the above form since the numerator $(-1)$ is a factor of $2$ and the denominator $(1)$ is a factor of $3.$
